title: 86% of These Small Businesses Use AI. Only 15% Made It Work
content:
In Goldman Sachs' survey of 2,400+ small business owners, eighty six percent now use AI.
But only fifteen percent have fully integrated it into their core operations.
That gap is the biggest opportunity in AI right now.
Yesterday, Goldman Sachs announced the Small Business AI Institute.
It is part of a new five hundred million dollar commitment to its 10,000 Small Businesses program.
And the partners are Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI.
Now look at the survey behind it.
Goldman surveyed more than two thousand four hundred graduates of the program.
Eighty six percent said they use AI in their business, up from fifty six percent in 2024.
But only fifteen percent said AI is fully integrated into their core operations.
And more than three quarters said they could use more training and resources.
So what does that tell us?
Using AI is not the same as integrating AI.
Asking a chatbot to write an email is using AI.
Having invoices, enquiries and reports flow through a system every day, with a human checking the important steps, is integration.
So how does a business move from the eighty six to the fifteen?
Step ONE. Pick one painful task that repeats every week, like answering the same customer questions.
Step TWO. Write down every step a person takes today.
Step THREE. Automate the boring steps, but keep a human approval on anything that touches money or customers.
Step FOUR. Measure the hours saved after one month.
Imagine a clinic that spends six hours a week replying to appointment enquiries. Even saving half of that is a real result you can show.
Here's my take. The tools are already here. What is missing is the person who connects them to real work.
If you are an engineer, that gap is your job market. If you run a business, that gap is your advantage.
